Render a camera path

Source: R/animate-3d.R
animate_3d.Rd

Render a fixed scene from successive camera positions. Geometry and scales are built once; projection, visibility and lighting are evaluated per frame.

Usage

animate_3d(
  plot,
  azimuth = NULL,
  elevation = NULL,
  zoom = NULL,
  frames = 60L,
  fps = 20,
  file = NULL,
  renderer = c("raster", "vector"),
  roll = NULL,
  width = 640L,
  height = 640L,
  dpi = 96,
  antialias = 1L,
  progress = interactive()
)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot with coord_3d().

azimuth, elevation, zoom, roll

A scalar, a numeric vector of length frames, or a function receiving times in seconds and returning either. NULL retains the plot setting, except azimuth, which makes one full turn.

frames

Number of frames, default 60. The closing view is excluded from the default turn so that looping repeats each view once.

fps

Frames per second, default 20.

file

Output path ending in .gif or .mp4. NULL returns PNG frame paths.

renderer

Scene backend, "raster" (default) or "vector". Both produce PNG frames for the encoder.

width, height

Frame dimensions in pixels, default 640 each.

dpi

Device resolution, default 96 dots per inch.

antialias

Raster supersampling factor, default 1.

progress

Report rendering time for each frame, default interactive().

Value

A ggplot3d_animation list with file, frame_count, fps, camera (one row per frame), timings in seconds, build_seconds, frame, panel_extents in millimetres, and frames (PNG paths when file is NULL). PNG frames returned with file = NULL belong to the caller.

Details

Framing is "azimuth" for constant elevation and roll, and "sphere" otherwise. Axis reserves and physical panel extents are fixed. Zoom remains an explicit magnification. GIF needs gifski; MP4 needs av. Optional packages are checked before rendering. Rendering streams frames to disk.

Examples

p <- ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(wt, mpg, z = hp)) +
  geom_point_3d() + coord_3d()
if (requireNamespace("gifski", quietly = TRUE)) {
  movie <- animate_3d(p, frames = 3, width = 320, height = 320,
                      file = tempfile(fileext = ".gif"))
  movie$timings
}
